messages.content:
You are FOXO's lifestyle coach. Using the doctor's review of a member's lab results, write a practical diet and lifestyle plan for a member living in India.

Rules:
1. Respect the member's diet, allergies and conditions in every item:
   - vegetarian: no meat, fish, seafood or eggs
   - eggetarian: eggs are fine; no meat, fish or seafood
   - vegan: no animal products, including dairy, ghee and honey
   - jain: vegetarian with no eggs, no honey, no onion or garlic, and no root vegetables (potato, carrot, beetroot, radish, ginger and similar)
   - allergies: never include the allergen in any form
   - diabetes: no sugar, jaggery, honey, sweets or sweetened drinks
2. Each diet recommendation must target one of the abnormal biomarkers in the doctor's findings. Put that biomarker's name in linked_biomarker, written as in the findings.
3. Never contradict the doctor's lifestyle_restrictions. If the doctor restricts exercise, suggest only gentle activity such as an easy walk, and tell the member to follow the doctor's advice.
4. Do not recommend medicines or supplements and never give doses. If a supplement might help, say "ask your FOXO doctor".
5. Use everyday Indian foods (dal, millets, seasonal sabzi, sprouts and so on) and be specific about portions and timing.
6. Put foods to eat in diet_recommendations and foods to limit or avoid in foods_to_avoid.
7. retest_in_weeks is usually 12.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"DietRecommendation": {"properties": {"item": {"title": "Item", "type": "string"}, "rationale": {"title": "Rationale", "type": "string"}, "linked_biomarker": {"title": "Linked Biomarker", "type": "string"}}, "required": ["item", "rationale", "linked_biomarker"], "title": "DietRecommendation", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"focus_areas": {"items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Focus Areas", "type": "array"}, "diet_recommendations": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/DietRecommendation"}, "title": "Diet Recommendations", "type": "array"}, "foods_to_avoid": {"default": [], "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Foods To Avoid", "type": "array"}, "activity": {"title": "Activity", "type": "string"}, "sleep": {"title": "Sleep", "type": "string"}, "retest_in_weeks": {"title": "Retest In Weeks", "type": "integer"}}, "required": ["focus_areas", "diet_recommendations", "activity", "sleep", "retest_in_weeks"], "title": "CoachPlan", "type": "object"}

response: {"focus_areas":["Raise low haemoglobin with iron-rich vegetarian foods and vitamin C at meals","Improve low vitamin D with fortified foods and safe morning sunlight","Keep activity gentle until haemoglobin is rechecked, as the doctor advised"],"diet_recommendations":[{"item":"At lunch and dinner, eat 1 katori (about 150 g cooked) dal or sprouted moong/chana, with a squeeze of lemon or a small tomato salad.","rationale":"Pulses give vegetarian iron, and lemon/tomato vitamin C helps your body absorb it better to support low haemoglobin.","linked_biomarker":"haemoglobin"},{"item":"Have 1 katori cooked seasonal green leafy sabzi (palak, methi or amaranth) 4–5 times a week, or 1/2 katori cooked beetroot in salad.","rationale":"Everyday Indian greens and beetroot add iron to a vegetarian diet and support low haemoglobin; pair them with lemon.","linked_biomarker":"haemoglobin"},{"item":"Take 1 tablespoon roasted pumpkin seeds or sesame seeds (til) as a mid-morning snack, or 1 tablespoon sesame chutney with lunch.","rationale":"Seeds are practical vegetarian iron sources for low haemoglobin; check labels for tree-nut cross-contamination because of your allergy.","linked_biomarker":"haemoglobin"},{"item":"Keep tea and coffee at least 1 hour away from meals; instead have lemon water, amla or guava as a snack.","rationale":"Tea and coffee can reduce iron absorption, while vitamin C foods help absorption and support low haemoglobin.","linked_biomarker":"haemoglobin"},{"item":"Have 1 glass (200–250 ml) vitamin D-fortified milk or curd daily as a mid-morning or evening snack; if using plant milk, choose a fortified soya option and check it has no tree nut.","rationale":"Fortified dairy or soya is a practical vegetarian vitamin D food; ask your FOXO doctor whether a supplement is needed for your low vitamin D.","linked_biomarker":"vitamin_d"},{"item":"Include 1 katori cooked mushrooms 3–4 times a week, for example in sabzi or soup.","rationale":"Mushrooms can provide some vitamin D, especially sun-exposed mushrooms, and add variety while you improve low vitamin D.","linked_biomarker":"vitamin_d"}],"foods_to_avoid":["Tree nuts and any food containing them — almond, cashew, pistachio, walnut, hazelnut, macadamia, pecan, Brazil nut, nut butters, cashew paste, nut-based sweets, gravies and bakery items; check labels strictly because of your tree-nut allergy.","Tea, coffee and cola with meals — keep at least a 1-hour gap before or after meals.","Packaged snacks, maida bakery items and sweets that may contain tree nuts — check labels before eating.","Nut-based milks, nut butters, cashew paste and nut-containing chutneys — avoid completely due to tree-nut allergy."],"activity":"Follow your doctor's restriction: no heavy lifting or high-intensity exercise until haemoglobin is rechecked. Try a gentle 10–15 minute easy walk after meals, and get 10–15 minutes of safe morning sunlight 3–4 times a week if your doctor agrees. Stop if you feel dizzy, breathless or very tired, and ask your FOXO doctor before increasing activity.","sleep":"Aim for 7–8 hours of sleep with a regular bedtime; keep screens away 30–60 minutes before bed. If you feel very tired or breathless, rest and contact your FOXO doctor.","retest_in_weeks":12}
